electricalAngleOfInverter2Against: Electrical angle of inverter 2 against inverter 1 (dual 3-phase is usually 30°). It changes the DC-link ripple, not the device losses.
rmsCurrentOfOnePhaseOne: RMS current of ONE phase (one inverter leg), continuous.
fundamentalElectricalFrequencyTheCarrier: Fundamental electrical frequency. The carrier is rounded to a whole number of periods of it (synchronous modulation).
displacementPowerFactorOfTheLoad: Displacement power factor of the load. Sets the power (and the efficiency), not the device losses.
thePowerDeviceFromTheCatalogue: The power device, from the catalogue below. Its card carries the datasheet numbers this solve uses.
dual3PhaseTheXY: Dual 3-phase: the x-y plane links no air-gap flux, only leakage limits its current. Required for two inverters — no field solve here measures it.
carrierPhaseShiftOfInverter2: Carrier phase shift of inverter 2 against inverter 1, 0–180° of a carrier period. Trades alpha-beta ripple against x-y ripple.
optionalPhaseCurrentThdPwmRipple: Optional: phase-current THD (PWM ripple / fundamental) above this is flagged FAIL.
howTheBridgesAreCombinedWith: How the bridges are combined with the motor: one inverter, two inverters on alternate coils, an H-bridge per coil, or an explicit coil-to-bridge mapping.
unipolarSwitchesTheTwoLegsAgainst: Unipolar switches the two legs against opposite references — the coil sees twice the ripple frequency and half the step. Bipolar switches the diagonals together.
gateOffVoltage0VOr: Gate-off voltage: 0 V or −5 V. It changes both the turn-off energy and the body-diode drop during dead time.
bothSwitchesOfALegOff: Both switches of a leg off. The current then runs through a SiC body diode at ~4 V, so this is expensive — and it is what distorts the output voltage at every current zero crossing.
liquidColdplateForcedAirFanSlipstream: Liquid coldplate, forced air (fan/slipstream) or still air (no fan) — the same three the thermal simulation offers for the housing, now for the device heatsink/plate.
howManyPlatesUsuallyOnePer: How many plates (usually one per module) the flow is split over or runs through. At least 2.
aHeatsinkBoltedToEachDevice: A heatsink bolted to EACH device, or one PCB pad shared by every device on it.
everyPublishedLimitOfTheChosen: Every published limit of the chosen device with the number this duty reaches. A line that is not judged is one the datasheet does not publish or this model does not compute — never a pass by omission.
whatTheCoilActuallySeesThe: What the coil actually sees: the PWM terminal voltage with the device drops and the dead-time windows, over the phase current. The voltage error the dead time causes flips sign at every current zero crossing.
everyBlockNeedsASourceLine: Every block needs a source line naming the table or figure it was transcribed from. A value the datasheet does not publish stays out — the loss model says so rather than guessing.

configureDrive.title: Drive
configureDrive.sineTip: Ideal sinusoidal current: no inverter, motor losses only.
configureDrive.pwmTip: A drive variant computed for this motor: a device at a carrier frequency, solved with the real inverter.
configureDrive.notComputed: PWM not computed for this motor — request calculation
configureDrive.notComputedTip: This machine's passport has no computed drive variants. Ask for the PWM calculation (Admin → Motors → Generate passport); Configure never calculates a device live.
configureDrive.variantTip: Only the drive variants computed for this motor are listed. Each is a device at a carrier frequency already in its passport.
configureDrive.buildTuned: PWM variants are computed for the loaded build. Reset turns, length and wire to read them.
configureDrive.buildTunedTip: A drive variant is solved for one winding, so only current and speed can move. Press Reset to reference design.
configureDrive.refuseSpeed: Refused: {rpm} rpm is outside the computed range {lo}–{hi} rpm
configureDrive.refuseCurrent: Refused: {amps} A is outside the computed range {lo}–{hi} A
configureDrive.refuseGap: Refused: no computed points around this operating point
configureDrive.refuseNoCoords: Refused: the variant's points carry no current or speed
configureDrive.refuseEnvelopeTip: Configure reads between the computed points of a drive variant and never outside them.
configureDrive.refuseTj: Refused: T_j {tj} °C is over the {limit} °C limit of {device}
configureDrive.refuseRating: Refused: {amps} A rms per switch is over the {limit} A rating of {device}
configureDrive.refuseVds: Refused: {device} blocks {vdss} V but the bus reaches {bus} V (at most {max} V allowed)
configureDrive.refuseBus: Refused: the pack reaches {pack} V, above the {max} V this variant was computed for
configureDrive.refuseLimitTip: A device limit is exceeded, so the numbers are withheld. Pick another variant or change the operating point.
configureDrive.motorLossTip: Total motor loss under this inverter at the operating point, read from the computed points.
configureDrive.invLossTip: Conduction + switching + dead time of every device in the bridge.
configureDrive.driveEffTip: Shaft power over battery power: motor losses and inverter losses both counted.
configureDrive.pContMaxTip: Largest continuous shaft power the variant holds at this speed.

configureLimits.connSeries: all series — highest voltage, lowest current
configureLimits.connParallel: all parallel — lowest voltage, highest current
configureLimits.connWarn: Line voltage {line} V is above the battery nominal {nominal} V
configureLimits.connWarnTip: At this operating point the winding needs a line peak of {line} V; the pack nominal is {nominal} V. The connection stays free: pick the other one or lower the speed.
configureLimits.overFit: Wire outside the stator — {stack} mm stack in a {avail} mm slot
configureLimits.overFitTip: {n} rows × ({wire} mm wire + {gap} mm gap) = {stack} mm; the slot leaves {slot} mm − 2×{ins} mm insulation = {avail} mm. Lower the turns or the wire thickness.
configureLimits.badTurns: {n} wires is not a whole number of {k}-in-hand turns
configureLimits.badTurnsTip: This build is wound {k} wires in hand, so the slot's wire count must be a multiple of {k}: {n} wires would make {turns} turns per coil, which is not a winding. Use {lo} or {hi}.
configureLimits.atLimitTip: {n} rows × ({wire} mm wire + {gap} mm gap) = {stack} mm of {avail} mm usable slot height — the sliders stop here so the winding stays inside the stator.
configureLimits.stockTip: Compared against the flat wire physically on the shelf (Materials tab → Flat wire in stock). Not enforced yet.
configureLimits.lHand: max {max} mm · set for this motor
configureLimits.lHandTip: The stack-length maximum was set by hand for this motor (admin). Admins edit it here; it applies to every user.
configureLimits.lDefaultTip: No maximum is set for this motor, so the default rule applies (a multiple of the reference length). An admin can set one by editing the maximum.
configureLimits.clearHandTip: Remove the hand-set maximum and fall back to the default rule.
configureLimits.nFitTip: The most wire rows that fit the slot at {wire} mm wire ({avail} mm usable height). The maximum follows the wire thickness live.
configureLimits.wireFitTip: Minimum 0.2 mm (manufacturing limit), step 0.1 mm. The maximum is the thickest wire at which the chosen turns still fit the slot.
configureLimits.iInverterTip: The machine's own inverter: the device's continuous rating ({rating} A at {tcase} °C case, junction at its limit) × devices in parallel, as a phase current. Applies in Sine mode too.
configureLimits.iNoControllerTip: No inverter device is saved with this machine, so the passport rule applies for the current maximum.
configureLimits.rpmEnvelopeTip: Highest speed at which the passport's voltage model, at the current set here, stays within the fully charged pack × modulation index {m}.
configureLimits.rpmKvTip: Kv × fully charged pack voltage × modulation index {m} (the passport has no voltage model).
configureLimits.rpmNoBatteryTip: No pack voltage is known for this machine, so the default rule applies for the speed maximum.
configureLimits.resetToReferenceTip: Put every knob back to the reference design (the motor as loaded)
